title: Bridge Closure in Mesh Topology
description: This scenario explores bridge closure dynamics within a mesh communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Freight must be rerouted through longer path
Agents at east depot may become isolated
Capacity bottleneck at east-north route due to rerouting
Information asymmetry: Agent A knows bridge is closed, Agent D does not
Race condition: Multiple agents attempting to use the single-capacity east-north route simultaneously
coordination_challenges: Dynamic re-routing synchronization: Ensuring agents do not commit to the same restricted route simultaneously
Priority-based resource contention: Negotiating access to the limited capacity 'east-north' corridor
Information propagation latency: Maintaining a consistent global world-state across the mesh topology during physical disruptions
Congestion management: Preventing deadlock at the 'south' depot as redirected traffic converges
agent_strategies: Distributed Consensus: Agents use the mesh topology to broadcast route status updates to achieve a shared belief of the network state
Reservation-based Routing: Agents reserve capacity on the east-north route in advance to prevent collisions
Priority Preemption: Low-priority agents yield the single-capacity route to high-priority 'med-kit' or 'food' carriers
Predictive Rerouting: Using the disturbance schedule to proactively divert agents before they reach the closed bridge

coordination_challenges: Freight must be rerouted through longer path

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Zero deadlocks encountered at single-capacity nodes
